value.text:
Two distinct paths handle the SignIn RPC.

`APIV1Service.SignIn` in `auth_service.go` implements the SignIn RPC. The gRPC-Gateway path registers it directly via `RegisterAuthServiceHandlerServer`. The Connect path delegates to it through `ConnectServiceHandler.SignIn`.

The definitive answer is `APIV1Service.SignIn` — `server/router/api/v1/auth_service.go`. This is the core handler containing the actual SignIn implementation.

`ConnectServiceHandler` embeds `*APIV1Service` and registers the auth service via `apiv1connect.NewAuthServiceHandler`. This appears to be the backend handler for the SignIn RPC.

`ConnectServiceHandler` defines its own `SignIn` method in `connect_services.go`, overriding the inherited `APIV1Service.SignIn`. The Connect version uses Connect request/response types, while the protobuf version uses gRPC types.

`APIV1Service.SignIn` in `auth_service.go` is the canonical backend handler. It implements the gRPC-gateway RPC and is registered via `RegisterAuthServiceHandlerServer`. `ConnectServiceHandler.SignIn` in `connect_services.go` is the Connect RPC handler.

The answer is `APIV1Service.SignIn — server/router/api/v1/auth_service.go`. This is the canonical gRPC service implementation. The Connect handler in `connect_services.go` is merely a thin adapter.

q04.

**APIV1Service.SignIn — server/router/api/v1/auth_service.go**

The `SignIn` RPC is defined on `AuthService` in `proto/api/v1/auth_service.proto`. On the backend, it is implemented by `APIV1Service.SignIn` in `server/router/api/v1/auth_service.go`, which performs password and SSO authentication and returns tokens.

That method is registered as the gRPC-Gateway handler in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go` via `RegisterAuthServiceHandlerServer`. Connect clients hit a thin wrapper, `ConnectServiceHandler.SignIn` in `server/router/api/v1/connect_services.go`, which delegates to `APIV1Service.SignIn`.
